correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, 0<tau<=n, uniqueness and S_n invariance force a shape a(I-H)+bH and center t*1. Direct support inequalities are s^2=((n-1)a+b)/n<=min(t,1-t)^2 and nt+sqrt(nb)<=tau. Uniqueness excludes t>1/2 by shifting to 1/2. Optimizing a and b at fixed t yields b=min(t^2,n(tau/n-t)^2), followed by an increasing branch and a globally unimodal branch with derivative zero at t=tau/(n+1). The resulting clipped center and b give all three formulas and both sharp boundaries. Exact facet support equalities give contact counts. The independently executed standard-library verifier passed 5,520 rational support cases and 248 grid tests. Finite verification is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The uniform-matroid independence polytope and real capped-hypercube interpolation form a canonical geometry family. The exact John ellipsoid, off-center-to-centered transition at (n+1)/2, anisotropic branch, return to a Euclidean ball at (n+sqrt(n))/2, and complete 2n+1 contact-facet pattern are not determined by Ehrhart or Euclidean inball data. The intermediate branch is a genuinely positive-length interval for every n>=2, with explicit volume and metric semiaxes; this is a natural complete classification rather than an unmotivated sample.
